samples.summary: Named-style exception leaves a new dead flag when the block later changes style, and nothing re-normalizes it
samples.evidence: `styleOffAsClear` intentionally keeps an explicit `false` where the block's named style supplies the key truthy (Heading 6 → italic). The stored `false` is only meaningful *for that style*: `setBlockType`/`updateStyleDefinition` can change a block to `paragraph`/`normal` (memory.ts:248 re-materializes block spacing on a StyleId change, and yorkie-doc-store.ts:1379 mirrors it), after which the run carries exactly the dead flag this change exists to eliminate — permanently un-mergeable by `normalizeInlines` and pinned against a later redefinition. The design doc's 'Out of scope' paragraph (docs/design/docs/docs-font-controls.md:280) only excuses flags written by *older builds*, not ones this branch still writes and then orphans. No inline-style normalization runs on the StyleId-change path (searched `blockStyleId(` call sites, memory.ts setBlockType/updateStyleDefinition, rematerializeDocSpacing).

samples.summary: styleOffAsClear re-implements the existing `caretStyleDefaults` helper instead of reusing it
samples.evidence: `model/caret-style.ts:31-40` already exposes `caretStyleDefaults(doc, position)` = `findBlock` + `resolveStyleInline(blockStyleId(block), doc.document.styles)` with the exact same header/footer/cell-lookup rationale documented in its comment. `styleOffAsClear` duplicates that three-line resolution (and the new `named-styles` import in `document.ts`) rather than calling it, so the two copies can drift if the defaults layer ever gains another source (e.g. table-cell or header context defaults). Reuse of the existing resolver would keep one definition of 'the layer painted under a run'.

samples.summary: Design-doc claim that 'every' boolean toggle-off is cleared is stronger than what the code enforces — the `applyStyles` batch path bypasses `Doc`
samples.evidence: The new invariant section asserts the guarantee 'holds across the docs engine … and the Yorkie store', with the demotion 'happening once' in `Doc.applyInlineStyle`/`applyInlineStyleToCells`. But `DocStore.applyStyles` (store.ts:90) is called directly from `view/editor.ts:1095` and `view/text-box-editor.ts:907`, skipping `Doc` and therefore `styleOffAsClear`. Today those sites only write `fontSize`, so the invariant is currently intact, but it is documented as a store-wide invariant while being enforced only on one of two write paths, with nothing (type, assertion, or comment on `applyStyles`) preventing a future boolean batch write from re-introducing the dead flag. Either narrow the doc's wording or enforce the demotion at the store boundary.

samples.summary: Storage-layer invariant filed under the font-controls UI doc rather than the named-styles / docs engine doc
samples.evidence: The added section is a model-level *storage* invariant about inline runs and the named-style cascade, but it lands in `docs-font-controls.md` — a shipped-UI doc about family/size/line-spacing pickers (its Goals, lines 30-46, are all toolbar controls). The cascade it depends on is specified in `docs/design/docs/docs-named-styles.md` ('Cascade resolution model', lines 117-131), which is the canonical home for 'defaults layered under the run style' and is not updated. Placement is defensible (the `CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE` clearing convention is already described here at lines 229-242) and it correctly avoids creating a parallel doc, so this is taste rather than a discipline violation.
